newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Citibank sees yuan rules clarified in 30-60 days.
newsitem.headline: Citibank sees yuan rules clarified in 30-60 days.

text.p: Citibank is optimistic that regulations governing Chinese yuan business will be in place in 30 to 60 days, said Stephen Long, country corporate officer for Citibank Hong Kong and North Asia division head.
"We have talked with the People's Bank of China, but have not gotten all the regulations. That will take place over the next 30 to 60 days," said Long, adding, "We are very optimistic."
Long said Citibank expects to open its doors for business within that time period. The bank is likely to turn a profit from yuan business shortly after operations begin, he added.
Citibank is one of four foreign banks that have been given approval to engage in local currency business in China's Pudong.
Hongkong and Shanghai Bank, Tokyo-Mitsubishi Bank and the Industrial Bank of Japan also were granted licences.
Long said he expects that China might revise tax rules for foreign banks, which currently pay 15 percent in income taxes.
That rate is far lower than the 33 percent paid by Chinese commercial shareholding banks and the 55 percent paid by state banks.
Long said he believed yuan business would be profitable even if tax rates were raised.
Citibank has about 200 employees in China, 75 of them in Shanghai. The bank is in the process of moving Shanghai employees to Pudong, said Long.
Banks engaging in yuan business must set up their main branch in Pudong. Citibank will maintain a sub-branch in Shanghai, said Long.
